module: Small profiling tool: measures durations in milliseconds with HighPerfTimer, either a single measurement (startMeasurement / stopMeasurement) or an average over N measurements written to the log (measureAverage).
usage:
local pl = extensions.performanceLogger
pl.startMeasurement('monCode')
-- ... code to measure ...
pl.measureAverage('monCode', 100)  -- log after 100 measurements
notes: measureAverage stops the named timer, accumulates, then after stopCount measurements writes a log 'name: x ms (avg over N measurements)' and resets the accumulation. startMeasurement must be called again before each measurement (it resets the timer).
showMin = true displays the minimum of the averages already observed instead of the current average.
Anomaly: the result is formatted with '%.5f' from a string (tostring); works thanks to LuaJIT's numeric string conversion.
Misspelled names are kept as is in the code: stopAvergage (without the 'a' before 'g').
measureAverage/stopMeasurement raise a Lua error if startMeasurement has not been called with that name.

onInit.desc: Initialization hook: clears timers and measurements.

stopMeasurement.desc: Stops the timer and returns the measured duration.

measureAverage.desc: Stops the timer, adds the measurement to the average and, after stopCount measurements, writes the average to the log.

showMin.desc: Display the minimum of the averages.

stopAvergage.desc: Ends the named average and returns the accumulated average (removes the timer).
